Promoting Fundamental British Values.

Pupils are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is "right" and "wrong", all people living in England are subject to its law.

pageCache.text:
St John's C of E Primary School Vision
St John's is an inspiring, safe, and inclusive place where ALL can thrive and succeed.
We already have an agreed set of Core Values that we are not planning to change – Kindness, Honesty, Perseverance, Respect & Responsibility. Our vision is informed by these values and by being a church school with a Christian ethos.
Our vision is for an inspiring, growing school where all children are welcome; a small school that is embedded in the village community, making the best use of our considerable local resources to develop children that are confident, motivated learners that are proud of their school, feel safe and achieve to the best of their ability.
The school will work in partnership with parents and carers to develop children’s spiritual and emotional well-being. We offer a curriculum that will not just ensure everyone succeeds in the key skills of maths and English, but will also enrich children's wider knowledge through creative and sports activities and experiences that prepare them for future life in the wider world.
Reviewed September 2025

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome | St John's C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome to St John’s Church of England Primary School, Tisbury
A very warm welcome to St John's!
It is a real privilege to be the Headteacher of St John's, a wonderful village school nestled in the beautiful Wiltshire countryside, where children are at the heart of everything we do.
I believe that primary school should be a special time in a child's life. A time to discover, explore, make friendships, develop confidence and, most importantly, develop a lifelong love of learning. Every child deserves to feel happy, safe, valued and excited about coming to school each day.
At St John's, we are fortunate to have something rather special. We are a small school with a big heart, where every child is known as an individual, relationships really matter and there is a genuine sense of family and belonging. Our beautiful grounds, including our Forest School, pond, allotment and extensive outdoor spaces, provide wonderful opportunities for children to explore, be curious, take risks and learn beyond the classroom.
The ambition is simple: for every child to feel that they belong, to believe in themselves and to achieve more than they ever thought possible.
I am passionate about providing an education that combines high expectations with kindness, nurture and understanding. I believe that children thrive when they feel secure, when their successes are celebrated and when they are encouraged to persevere, challenge themselves and have a go, even when things feel difficult.
We want our children to be confident, curious and independent learners who are not afraid to ask questions, make mistakes or think differently. Through high-quality teaching, a rich and engaging curriculum and meaningful experiences, we aim to inspire every child to discover their strengths, develop new interests and achieve their very best.
Equally important to me is children's emotional wellbeing. We recognise that every child is unique and that children arrive at school with different experiences, strengths and needs. Our inclusive and nurturing approach means that we take time to understand each child, helping them develop the confidence, resilience and emotional skills they need to flourish, both in school and in the wider world.
As a Church of England school, our Christian ethos is woven through everyday school life. Our core values of Kindness, Honesty, Perseverance, Respect and Responsibility help shape the way we learn, behave and care for one another. We want our children not only to achieve academically, but also to grow into thoughtful, compassionate and responsible young people who understand the difference they can make in the world.
One of the greatest strengths of St John's is our community. I firmly believe that the best outcomes for children happen when school and home work together. I value open, honest communication and positive relationships with parents and carers. We want families to feel welcome, listened to and involved in their child's school journey. We are also proud of our strong links with the church, our village and the wider community, which enrich the experiences we can offer our children.
Alongside our dedicated staff and governors, I am excited about continuing to develop St John's, building on everything that makes our school special while always looking for ways to make it even better. We will celebrate our successes, embrace new opportunities and never stop asking ourselves what more we can do for the children in our care.
Above all, St John's is a place where childhood is celebrated, learning is exciting, everyone belongs and every child has the opportunity to shine.
Of course, a website can only tell you so much about a school. The best way to understand what makes St John's special is to come and experience it for yourself. I would be delighted to welcome you, show you around and introduce you to the wonderful children and staff who make our school what it is.
I look forward to meeting you.
Mrs Lisa Ashford-Smith NPQH, NPQLBC
DSL / SENCo Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Personal, Social, Health and Emotional Learning (PSHE) / Relationships and Sex Education (RSE)
At St. John's we use PSHE curriculum from the leading children's health and well-being charity, Coram LIfe Education. We value each child for who they are, encourage children to embrace their unique talents and teach transferable skills to support learning. Our aim is to prepare children to take their place in a diverse society. This is all underpinned by our whole-school Thrive approach.
Our whole-school PSHE topics are:
Term 1: Me & My Relationships
Term 2: Valuing Difference
Term 3: Keeping Safe
Term 4: Rights & Respect
Term 5: Being My Best
Term 6: Growing & Changing
Please see the documents below for further information on PSHE/SCARF at St. John's, including RSE.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music at St John's | St John's C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
Music at St John's
Here at St John's we love music.
We love to sing, we love to listen and we love to play.
Each class has a music lesson once a week where we get to listen, compose, perform, improvise and find out about the history of music.
We sing as a whole school in every assembly and enjoying learning about a new musician every month. This year we are going to meet a wide range of musicians, from Jimi Hendrix to Handel!
Our Musician of the Month means that we get to experience a wide-range of music from all over the world. We can discuss how the music makes us feel and find out about the lives of the fascinating musicians that we meet. YouTube and Spotify playlists are available so familes can join in with the fun at home if they wish!
You'll also hear singing coming from our classrooms - whether it's times tables, nouns or the continents of the world, we love to sing to support our learning.
Each class will get the chance to learn the ukelele and the recorder at St John's so you may even hear whole classes playing together in beautiful harmony.
Individual instrumental lessons are available for trumpet, ukelele and recorder - if you are interested in this please contact the office.
